is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses exclusively on Culex quinquefasciatus, as stated in the title and throughout the text (e.g., page 1: 'Ugandan Culex quinquefasciatus populations').

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes Vgsc-1014F (L995F) and Ace1-119S (G280S) (page 1, Abstract; page 8, Table 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts (RR/RS/SS) and sample sizes (N) for both markers are provided in Table 1 on page 8.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Uganda (Jinja, Kampala, Kanungu, and Tororo) in 2012 (page 3, 'Area of study and mosquito collection'; page 4, 'between July and August 2012').

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article reporting original genotyping and population genetic analysis.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for specific districts and cities: Jinja, Kampala, Kanungu, and Tororo (page 8, Table 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted within a single two-month window between July and August 2012 (page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study mentions sample collection was supported by NIAID Award Number U19AI089674 (ICEMR), but the genotype data for these Culex populations appears to be original to this publication.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and sample sizes are provided in Table 1 of the main manuscript.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the frequency of insecticide resistance markers (Vgsc-1014F and Ace1-119S) in Culex quinquefasciatus populations across four districts in Uganda to determine if selection pressure from malaria control interventions (targeting Anopheles) affects non-target species. While it provides extractable genotype data for target markers, it is ineligible because it does not study Anopheles mosquitoes.
exclusion_reasons: Does not study Anopheles mosquitoes (focuses on Culex quinquefasciatus).
